newsitem.title: FRANCE: France gloomy about economy ahead of vote - poll.
newsitem.headline: France gloomy about economy ahead of vote - poll.

text.p: French voters have become gloomier about the state of the economy ahead of a May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, according to a BVA poll made public on Tuesday.
The poll for the business monthly Enjeux Les Echos found 79 percent were unhappy with the economic situation in France, compared with 76 percent the previous month.
Just 18 percent were pleased with the state of the economy, down four percent from March.
More than eight in 10 voters said they were unhappy with the social climate in France.

Thirty-nine percent said the economic picture would worsen in months ahead, up from 37 percent last month, while 40 percent said the picture would remain unchanged, 18 percent said things would get better and three percent had no opinion, BVA said.
Ninety-five percent said they were unhappy with the employment picture in France, where the jobless rate is at a record high of 12.8 percent.

The opinion poll was based on telephone interviews with 955 people aged 18 and over and was conducted on April 4-5, before Conservative President Jacques Chirac called a parliamentary election 10 months ahead of the normal deadline.
Nearly half said they thought the unemployment rate would deteriorate further in months ahead, while just 15 percent believed it would improve.
The remainder said they thought it would remain unchanged or had no opinion.
Asked whether they thought taxes would go up in months ahead, 62 percent said they would rise while 10 percent said they saw them falling. Twenty-five percent saw taxes remaining at current levels.
The centre-right government says it has no plans to raise taxes and is committed to reducing payroll tax.

After pledging to cut tax in his 1995 presidential campaign, Chirac and his allies in the centre-right government have raised value added tax (VAT) by two percent to 20.6 percent, while starting to bring down income tax over a five-year period from this year.
